title: How they treat the waiter
header_line: My analysis of one book on an entrepreneur's life. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: How do you treat people who can't help you?

A student said: if I walk into a big dinner you are hosting, and I see you are respectful to the waiter and the staff, focused on the guests and the conversation, that is a big tell. It is the way people treat people who aren't superior to them or who aren't their boss.
In an interview or partnership meeting everyone is on their best behaviour, the student said, but how do they treat their everyday interactions?

I said that I have seen leaders who have that magic, like an aura. They get out of a car at a hotel and say hello to everybody on their way to reception. They engage them and look in their eyes. People think: that is an important person, just because they acknowledge everyone around them at all times.
These great leaders' common denominator is the ability to connect with people in seconds. People think: there's something special. I feel I could sit down and talk to this person, I said.
Who greets everyone in your office, and who doesn't?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write how you greet the person at reception.
Write how you treat people who cannot help you.
Write a leader you know who acknowledges everyone.
Write what you could do differently tomorrow.
Write how you will notice it in a partner.
